# Problem 1

```{r}

data("ny_noaa")
```

This data set from the NOAA displays daily observed weather from all New York State weather stations, January 1, 1981 to December 31, 2010. The seven key variables include the station ID, date, precipitation, snowfall, snow depth, daily temperature high, and daily temperature low. The table dimensions are `r nrow(ny_noaa)` by `r ncol(ny_noaa)`, with all data missing in the first ten rows.

```{r}

ny_noaa_df = 
  ny_noaa |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  mutate(
    year = year(date),    # e.g., 2007
    month = month(date, label = TRUE),  # 1-12
    day = day(date),     # 1-31
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )

snow_counts = 
  ny_noaa_df |>
  count(snow) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

### Analyzing the Cleaned Data Set

Looking at the most commonly observed values after cleaning the data set, 0mm of snowfall appears `r snow_counts |> filter(snow == 0) |> pull(n) |> format(big.mark = ",")` times, likely due to the fact that it rarely snows outside of the winter months. The second more commonly observed value is NA, totaling `r snow_counts |> filter(is.na(snow)) |> pull(n) |> format(big.mark = ",")` times, as many weather stations across New York State do not report snowfall. The next eight most commonly observed values are 25, 13, 51, 76, 8, 5, 38, and 3 (in mm).

### Creating a Two-Panel Average Maximum Temperature Plot for January and July

```{r}

ny_noaa_df |> 
  filter(month %in% c("Jan", "Jul")) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) + 
  geom_point(aes(color = id), alpha = .1) + 
  labs(
    title = "Average January vs. July Maximum Temperatures by Weather Station",
    x = "Year (1981-2010)",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (C)",
    caption = "Data from the rnoaa package") +
  geom_line(aes(color = id), alpha = .1) +
  facet_grid(month ~ .) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Plotting each station’s average maximum temperature for January and July from 1981 to 2010 shows that January is consistently colder than July. January averages generally fall between about -10°C and 10°C, while July averages fall between about 20°C and 33°C. January also varies more from year to year than July. In both months, the stations tend to rise and fall together. For example, nearly every station had a colder-than-usual January in 1994 and 2004 and a warmer January in 1990 and 2006, which suggests the year-to-year changes reflect regional weather patterns. A few notable outliers include one station that averaged a maximum of about 14°C in July 1988 and another that averaged about -13°C in January 1982.

### Creating Plots for Temperature and Snowfall

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.asp = 1}

ggp_tmax_tmin = 
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) + 
  geom_hex() +
   labs(
    title = "Maximum vs. Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (°C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (°C)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right") +
  coord_fixed()

ggp_snowfall = 
  ny_noaa_df |> 
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(year), y = snow)) + 
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Between 1981 and 2010",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Snowfall (mm)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))

ggp_tmax_tmin / ggp_snowfall
```

# Problem 2

### Organizing Demographic and Accelerometer Data Sets

```{r}

nhanes_covar_df = 
  read_csv(file = "./data/nhanes_covar.csv", na = c("NA", ".", ""), skip = 4) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    sex = 
      case_match(
        sex, 
        1 ~ "male", 
        2 ~ "female"),
    education =
      case_match(
        education,
        1 ~ "less than high school",
        2 ~ "high school",
        3 ~ "more than high school"),
    education = factor(education, levels = c("less than high school", "high school", "more than high school"))) |>
  filter(age >= 21) |>
  drop_na(age, education, sex)

nhanes_covar_df |>
  count(sex, education) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex, 
    values_from = n) |>
  knitr::kable()
    
nhanes_covar_df |>
  mutate(sex = forcats::fct_relevel(sex, c("male", "female"))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = education, y = age)) + 
  geom_violin(aes(fill = sex), color = "blue", alpha = .5) + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education Level",
    x = "Education",
    y = "Age (years)",
    fill = "Sex"
  )
